subproblem.title: Mass controls evaluation: mass-null sequences tend weakly to 0, mass-summable series converge weakly, and the mass of the weak sum is at most the sum of the masses
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let X_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (j ∈ ℕ). (i) If M(X_j) → 0 in [0, ∞], then X_j(ω) → 0 in ℝ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U). (ii) If Σ_j M(X_j) < ∞ (tsum in [0, ∞]), then (a) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) the real series Σ_j X_j(ω) is summable, and (b) every Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that Σ_j X_j(ω) = Y(ω) (HasSum) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) satisfies M(Y) ≤ Σ_j M(X_j). Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)); for U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^n(U) = TestFormOn U n (smooth n-forms on ℝ^P whose compact tsupport lies in U) and 𝒟_n(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U n (SimonGMT Chapter06), X(ω) the value of X on ω. |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector. M_G(X) = X.massOn G ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over the ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (such ω are admissible for M_G, massAdmissibleOn U n G); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X). HasSum is unconditional summation in ℝ; Σ_j M(X_j) is the tsum in [0, ∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n), (Tendsto (fun j => (X j).mass) atTop (𝓝 0) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Tendsto (fun j => X j ω) atTop (𝓝 0)) ∧ (∑' j, (X j).mass < ∞ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Summable (fun j => X j ω)) ∧ ∀ Y : GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, HasSum (fun j => X j ω) (Y ω)) → Y.mass ≤ ∑' j, (X j).mass)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps (0d) and (8a) of the parent's supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1: mass convergence of the deformed pieces gives their weak convergence in (19), and the mass of the limit is estimated as in (25); chapter-06.txt lines 1792–1838), stated for an arbitrary domain U. Siblings used: CB = cmc_fc_sc_testForm_coeff_bound (key coeff_bound): every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) has a real c > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ c for all x ∈ ℝ^P; EB = cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn (key eval_mass_bound): if M_W(T) ≠ ∞, tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ r for all x, then |T(ω)| ≤ r·M_W(T).toReal.
1. (Evaluation bound.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), r ∈ ℝ with |ω(x)| ≤ r for every x, and j ∈ ℕ with M(X_j) ≠ ∞. Since ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, tsupport ω ⊆ U (the second component of the membership proof, ω.property.2), and M(X_j) = M_U(X_j) by the definition of mass. EB with W := U gives |X_j(ω)| ≤ r·M(X_j).toReal.
2. (Proof of (i).) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and choose c > 0 by CB. Since M(X_j) → 0 and 0 < 1, eventually M(X_j) < 1 < ∞, so eventually M(X_j) ≠ ∞ and, by step 1 with r := c, |X_j(ω)| ≤ c·M(X_j).toReal. The map ENNReal.toReal is continuous at 0 (because 0 ≠ ∞; ENNReal.tendsto_toReal) and 0.toReal = 0, so M(X_j).toReal → 0 and hence c·M(X_j).toReal → c·0 = 0. By the squeeze theorem for norms (squeeze_zero_norm', with ‖X_j(ω)‖ = |X_j(ω)|), X_j(ω) → 0.
3. (Finiteness in (ii).) Assume Σ_j M(X_j) < ∞. Then M(X_j) ≠ ∞ for every j (ENNReal.ne_top_of_tsum_ne_top), the real series Σ_j M(X_j).toReal is summable (ENNReal.summable_toReal), and Σ_j M(X_j).toReal = (Σ_j M(X_j)).toReal (ENNReal.tsum_toReal_eq, all terms finite).
4. (Proof of (ii)(a).) Fix ω and c > 0 from CB. By steps 1 and 3, ‖X_j(ω)‖ = |X_j(ω)| ≤ c·M(X_j).toReal for every j, and Σ_j c·M(X_j).toReal is summable (Summable.mul_left). By comparison (Summable.of_norm_bounded), Σ_j X_j(ω) is summable.
5. (Proof of (ii)(b).) Let Y be as in (b). By definition, M(Y) = M_U(Y) is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal Y(ω) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, so (sSup_le) it suffices to show ENNReal.ofReal Y(ω) ≤ Σ_j M(X_j) for every admissible ω, i.e. for ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ U and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Fix such an ω. By step 1 with r := 1, |X_j(ω)| ≤ M(X_j).toReal for all j, so Σ_j |X_j(ω)| is summable by comparison with the summable series of step 3 (Summable.of_nonneg_of_le). Since HasSum (X_j(ω))_j (Y(ω)), we have Y(ω) = Σ_j X_j(ω) (HasSum.tsum_eq), and termwise comparison of summable series (Summable.tsum_le_tsum, twice) gives Y(ω) = Σ_j X_j(ω) ≤ Σ_j |X_j(ω)| ≤ Σ_j M(X_j).toReal = (Σ_j M(X_j)).toReal (step 3). Since ENNReal.ofReal is monotone and ENNReal.ofReal((Σ_j M(X_j)).toReal) = Σ_j M(X_j) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, the sum being finite), ENNReal.ofReal Y(ω) ≤ Σ_j M(X_j). Taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M(Y) ≤ Σ_j M(X_j). ∎
Lean note (compiled route, about 45 lines): `Submission.cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn P n U U (X j) ω r hj ω.property.2 hr` gives step 1; in step 2 use `(hlim.eventually (gt_mem_nhds zero_lt_one)).mono` for the eventual finiteness, `(ENNReal.tendsto_toReal ENNReal.zero_ne_top).comp hlim` followed by `rw [ENNReal.toReal_zero]`, and `squeeze_zero_norm'`; in step 5 start with `refine sSup_le ?_; rintro _ ⟨ω, hω, rfl⟩`, so that hω.2 is the pointwise bound by 1, and finish with `rw [← ENNReal.tsum_toReal_eq hfin, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal hsum.ne]`.
proof_key_steps: EB with W := U and the bound |ω(x)| ≤ c of CB give |X_j(ω)| ≤ c·M(X_j).toReal whenever M(X_j) < ∞.
(i): M(X_j) is eventually finite and M(X_j).toReal → 0, so X_j(ω) → 0 by squeezing.
(ii)(a): Σ M(X_j) < ∞ makes Σ c·M(X_j).toReal summable, and comparison gives summability of Σ X_j(ω).
(ii)(b): for admissible ω, Y(ω) = Σ X_j(ω) ≤ Σ |X_j(ω)| ≤ Σ M(X_j).toReal = (Σ M(X_j)).toReal; take the supremum (sSup_le).
